trust_decision.summary: When Hurl follows a redirect to a different scheme/host/port (and --location-trusted is not set), credentials (Authorization, Cookie, --user) must not be forwarded; decided by should_strip_credentials_on_redirect and applied inside Client::execute_with_redirect, which filtered only request_spec.headers and options.user, not the [Cookies] list (request_spec.cookies) that libcurl sends via CURLOPT_COOKIE.

landing_point.why: The only redirect-following code with an explicit cross-host credential strip; the comment above it names Cookie headers and curl's CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION rule.

fix_sites.entry_point: hurl CLI with --location / [Options] location: true; public API hurl::runner::run; public API hurl::http::Client::execute_with_redirect

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The published fix touches only Client::execute_with_redirect (fix.diff:270-297); no source change lands in another module.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Headers from -H/--header, HURL_HEADER, the config file or an [Options] header: line are explicit user options 'meant for every request', merged later in configure() rather than part of the request's own headers, so a solver can argue they are a separate feature the [Cookies] report does not cover.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Same-origin redirects must still forward Authorization, Cookie header and [Cookies]; --location-trusted must forward everything to all hosts; non-credential -H/[Options] header: values (e.g. Accept, User-Agent) must survive the redirect; libcurl's domain-scoped cookie store (Set-Cookie cookies) must keep working; proxy headers go to the proxy only. An over-broad fix that drops all options.headers, clears the cookie engine, or strips on every redirect breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: [Cookies] section with one or more name/value entries (Vec<RequestCookie> joined with '; ')
Cookie request header in any letter case (already handled by name_eq at pinned commit; fix adds tests for lowercase 'cookie:')

O7_producer.where: packages/hurl/src/runner/request.rs:86-93 builds RequestSpec.cookies from the AST; packages/hurl/src/http/client.rs:678-688 turns it into CURLOPT_COOKIE, so the Cookie header is produced by libcurl and never appears in the header list the strip filters

O8_uncovered_routes.route: User-supplied global/per-entry headers (CLI -H/--header, HURL_HEADER env var, config file 'header', [Options] header:) are merged into the outgoing headers in configure() after the redirect strip, so Authorization/Cookie supplied this way still go to a different host.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: These are option-level headers, a neighbouring feature to the hurl-file [Cookies] section the report names; the strip at client.rs:142-143 looks complete because it already filters Authorization and Cookie.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Same file as the landing point for the merge, but the producers sit in packages/hurl/src/runner/options.rs:99-102, packages/hurl/src/cli/options/args.rs:498, packages/hurl/src/cli/options/env_vars.rs:118 and packages/hurl/src/cli/options/config_file/mod.rs:119

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A proxy/extra-credential header list (e.g. a per-request auth header option) applied in configure() rather than in the RequestSpec, bypassing the redirect strip.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: configure() already merges options.headers and proxy_headers late; a maintainer adding another header-producing option there would not think of the redirect loop.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another auth form (e.g. bearer section) stored as a dedicated RequestSpec field rendered by libcurl, like cookies, instead of an Authorization header.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: [Cookies] already follows this pattern (field + libcurl option) and is exactly what the strip missed.
